solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wide support for chair, one seen on TV?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a loose definition: a presenter is seen on television

parts.note: wide means broad
a caster is a small wheel on the leg of a chair

explanation.surface: A pun on someone who chairs a TV discussion being broadly supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support for chair' looks like backing for a committee chairman, but it is the little wheel under a chair's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presents radio or television programmes is commonly seen on screen, hence the hedged question mark.

clue.text: Boat's knocking out top boats

indicators.note: knocking out the top of a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: boat's read as craft's, with the possessive giving the S

explanation.surface: A vessel's crew knocking out the best of the other vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out top' removes C from CRAFT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafts are simple flat floating platforms, a basic kind of boat.

clue.text: Too controlled, as a nonentity

parts.note: too means also
to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: Someone too controlling to be noticed, like a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled' looks like restraint, but it is the past tense of run a company.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a loser in a race and so, figuratively, someone of no importance.

clue.text: Inquest lawyers having gold swapped for singers

indicators.note: swapped says the two gold letters change places

parts.note: coroners hold inquests into deaths, and are often lawyers
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Inquest officials trading gold to become singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapped' turns the OR in CORONERS into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooners are singers of sentimental ballads in a soft, low style, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Shy in boozer, put up with son

indicators.note: with places one piece beside the other
put up in a down entry means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A shy drinker in a pub, put up with his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, but it is a throw. 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy, so to shy is to fling something.

clue.text: Articles about performances

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and shuffled

explanation.surface: News pieces covering shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ARTICLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetic performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: It's vulgar. Going topless, it's just the same

definitions.text: It's vulgar. Going topless, it's just the same

parts.words: It's vulgar. Going topless, it's just the same
parts.note: a word for vulgarity which, with its first letter removed, still means vulgarity

explanation.surface: Commentary on someone going topless: vulgar either way.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its first letter the answer becomes RUDENESS, a synonym, hence 'just the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudeness is coarseness or vulgarity of manner, as is its beheaded form rudeness.

clue.text: Overseas territory in which friend has to keep personal pass

indicators.note: to keep says the friend holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
personal means one's own
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A distant land where a pal must hold a personal permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests a permit, but here it is a mountain gap; 'to keep' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown colony is a territory ruled directly by the British monarch's government, such as Hong Kong was.

clue.text: Mistake made by some vicar or reverend on retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left
some of the words means only part of their letters is used

explanation.surface: A slip committed by a clergyman while away at a spiritual retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks RORRE from 'vicaR OR REverend'; 'on retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a plain synonym for a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Rushes by rotten branches

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: food gone off is rotten
rushes means shoots, as in shoots past

explanation.surface: Rushes growing beside a decaying riverbank plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushes' looks like reeds, but it is the verb, dashes; 'by' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshoots are side growths of a plant, its branches, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Pirate looked around Lake District mountain

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps the other

parts.note: looked means saw
Captain William Kidd was a notorious pirate

explanation.surface: A buccaneer surveyed the scenery from a Cumbrian peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous national park in north-west England; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddaw is one of the highest fells in the Lake District, above Keswick.

clue.text: Performing arts popular when showing top Russian women

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of arts doing a turn, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashionable
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: The performing arts enjoying popularity among the Russian elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges ARTS to TSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives of the tsars, empresses, were the highest-ranking women in imperial Russia.

clue.text: To me to be without money is vexatious

indicators.note: to be without means to be outside, so the first word surrounds the money

parts.note: taken as written
roubles are Russian money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being penniless is a nuisance to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be without' is the container signal, with 'without' in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome is irritating or causing difficulty, just as vexatious things are.

clue.text: Wearing fashionable pants, that is wise

indicators.note: wearing says the rearranged pants enclose the next piece
fashionable read as fashioned, made into a new shape

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Wearing trendy trousers shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' is the anagram signal, giving SAPNT; 'Wearing' then wraps those letters round the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means having great wisdom or discernment, from Latin sapere, to be wise.

clue.text: Dodgy anagram about brandy

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of anagram are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A dubious word puzzle concerning brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' shuffles ANAGRAM to ARMAGNA; C for 'about' completes it. The clue's fodder is the word anagram itself, a cheeky touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy distilled in Gascony in south-west France.

clue.text: No restriction in port

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a ban is a restriction

explanation.surface: A harbour without any limits on entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish harbour town, a port for ferries to the Hebrides.

clue.text: Pal leaves perambulator around the trees

indicators.note: leaves says the friend's letters go out of the next word
around says the letters that remain are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend leaves a pram in a wooded park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes P, A, L from PERAMBULATOR; 'around' rearranges ERAMBUTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden or park where trees are grown for study and display.

clue.text: Fixes transfers

definitions.meaning: to fix a date or a task is to allot it
property or rights are handed over to another person

explanation.surface: A list of repairs and handovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is both to allot or fix something and, in law, to transfer property to another.

clue.text: At first, Australia bats terribly — batting second, resists

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter
terribly suggests the letters of bats are badly arranged

parts.note: a batsman batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Australia bat poorly, then batting second, they resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns BATS into BSTA. In cricket the side batting is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something, to resist the urge to indulge.

clue.text: 'He, Tarzan' out in town in Galilee

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Tarzan, introducing himself, spotted out in a Galilean town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HETARZAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth, in Galilee in northern Israel, is where Jesus grew up.

clue.text: Look after unusually extensive capital

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the next

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, an unusually large size
lo means look!

explanation.surface: An instruction to tend to some unusually large area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrase, take care of, but 'after' is the placing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Where honoured names are doing well

definitions.meaning: names of the honoured are inscribed ... of honour

explanation.surface: Honoured names doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally inscribed on a list such as an honours roll; idiomatically having a streak of success.

clue.text: Detective turns in criminal online in threatening place

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
criminal suggests the letters of online are crooked, out of order
turns says the detective's letters face the other way

parts.note: DS is Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A policeman goes undercover in the world of internet crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' gives LIONEN, 'turns' gives SD, and 'in' places the second within the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A lions' den, from the Bible story of Daniel, is a dangerous or hostile setting.

clue.text: Impetuous fellow's rip-off

parts.note: to rip is to tear
off means away, as in 'go off'

explanation.surface: A reckless man's swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' looks like a swindle, but it splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, reckless young person, especially a boy.

clue.text: Passage where ladies sleep regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter at even intervals

explanation.surface: A corridor where women sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and later alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: Timeless seasonal visitor coming over bumped into composer

indicators.note: coming over says the shortened visitor covers the next piece, sitting either side of it
less time means the letter T, the abbreviation for time, is removed

parts.note: Santa Claus visits at Christmas
bumped into means met by chance

explanation.surface: Father Christmas, bumping into someone who arrives, collides with a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' leaves SANA, which 'coming over' wraps round the meeting word; 'seasonal visitor' is the Christmas gift-bringer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Song — one from musical male dropped

indicators.note: dropped says the male letter falls out of the name

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of West Side Story and The Sound of Music

explanation.surface: A number from a musical, with the leading man cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes M from MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: E.g. Arab people with king in tights

parts.note: a race is a people

indicators.note: in says the king goes inside the tights

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An Arab, perhaps, among people with a king dressed in tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E.g. Arab' looks like a person, but the Arab is a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab, or Arabian, is a famous horse breed often raced, so it exemplifies the category.

clue.text: Grieve for an instant by receptacle for ashes

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
an urn holds a person's ashes

explanation.surface: Mourning briefly beside a funeral urn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets MO beside URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn is to grieve for someone who has died.

clue.text: Ploughman as investor

definitions.meaning: jokily, one who holds the share, the cutting blade of a plough
someone who owns stock in a company

explanation.surface: A farmer acting as a financial investor.
explanation.walkthrough: A share is also the blade of a plough, so whoever grips it is humorously a holder of the share.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor owns part of a company in units of stock; the ploughman holds a ploughshare.
